title: Form_Load reads a control's designer-set Text BEFORE running its custom initialisation. The VB6 runtime guarantees this; WinForms OnLoad has the same shape but Blazor OnInitializedAsync does NOT
sourceContent:
VERSION 5.00
Begin VB.Form frmGreet
   Caption         =   "Greeting"
   ClientHeight    =   3015
   Begin VB.TextBox txtName
      Text            =   "Anon"
      Height          =   375
   End
   Begin VB.Label lblHello
      Caption         =   ""
      Height          =   375
   End
End
Attribute VB_Name = "frmGreet"
Attribute VB_GlobalNameSpace = False

Private Sub Form_Load()
    ' VB6 GUARANTEE: controls are instantiated and their designer-set
    ' properties (e.g. txtName.Text = "Anon") are applied BEFORE this
    ' handler runs. The reads on the next two lines are safe.
    Dim defaultName As String
    defaultName = txtName.Text          ' Reads "Anon" — the designer default
    lblHello.Caption = "Hello, " & defaultName
End Sub

Private Sub txtName_Change()
    lblHello.Caption = "Hello, " & txtName.Text
End Sub

canonicalInputs.scenario: form opens with no user input
canonicalInputs.expected: lblHello.Caption = 'Hello, Anon' (designer default propagates via Form_Load read).
txtName_Change fires per keystroke; lblHello.Caption updates to 'Hello, World' on the final stroke.

notes: Classic VB6 lifecycle assumption. WinForms preserves the semantics (OnLoad runs after handle creation, before Shown) and the WinForms archetype's translation is a 1:1 port. Blazor Server's OnInitializedAsync, however, runs BEFORE the DOM exists — reading control state there is undefined. The extraction MUST emit (a) two event_handler_contract claims (Form_Load + txtName_Change), (b) a default_property_usage claim for the implicit txtName.Text access, and (c) an open_question naming the Blazor paradigm gap. A spec that flags only Form_Load and skips the Blazor caveat is a calibration miss for the Blazor target archetype specifically.
